solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old MacDonald's female branch?

definitions.note: a possessive standing for the thing the nursery-rhyme farmer owned, the place where he kept his animals

parts.note: an arm is a branch, as of a river, company or tree

explanation.surface: A jokey question about whether the nursery-rhyme farmer has a women's section.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's song says Old MacDonald had one, so his possession is the holding where the animals live.

clue.text: Sex-kittens initially follow men only

indicators.note: initially asks for just the opening letter of the hyphenated word Sex-kittens

parts.note: to tag along is to follow, so tag here means follow

explanation.surface: Pin-ups trail after a men-only crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party or stag night is an event restricted to male guests.

clue.text: Shortly, what central heating will reveal knocks?

definitions.text: Shortly, what central heating will reveal
definitions.meaning: central heating written short is C and H, the cold and hot markings on a pair of fixtures over a basin

explanation.surface: A question about the clanking pipes you hear once the heating starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' abbreviates central heating to C and H, the labels on cold and hot basin fittings.
explanation.definitionFit: Light blows on a door are raps, and the basin fittings share the same word.

clue.text: Dry recipe? I admitted, I love the food element

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so these pieces are taken inside the exclamation

parts.note: an exclamation of delight at tasty food is yum
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, i.e. dry
R is the abbreviation for recipe (Latin 'take') on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A diner admits liking the food despite a dull recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' puts TT, R and I inside YUM. The element is a rare-earth metal, symbol Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Yttrium is a chemical element, a silvery metal named after the Swedish village Ytterby.

clue.text: In office, superior mums in animated protest?

indicators.note: in places the mothers inside the rearranged letters
animated means lively and stirred up, so the letters of protest are jumbled

parts.note: mas are mums, mothers

explanation.surface: Mothers making a lively protest about their boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The superior in a post office is its head; 'In office' looks like 'holding a post' generally.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a post office is its head, the senior official there.

clue.text: Expert in spoken language successfully achieved MA

indicators.note: in speech signals that the words are judged by how they are pronounced

parts.note: having passed a Master of Arts degree, one has passed master

explanation.surface: An expert in linguistics who has gained a master's degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A past master is a thoroughly skilled person, an adept in some activity.

clue.text: Where you can see your ups and downs planned

definitions.text: Where you can see your ups and downs planned

parts.words: Where you can see your ups and downs planned
parts.note: a chart showing hills and valleys in raised form shows terrain highs and lows mapped out

explanation.surface: Sounds like a diary of life's emotional highs and lows.
explanation.walkthrough: Ups and downs suggest moods; here they are hills and valleys, and planned means drawn as a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of chart depicts the height of land, its hills and hollows, by shading or moulding.

clue.text: Feature of bread, toasted? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: toasted bread turns brown

explanation.surface: Asking whether a characteristic of bread is that it has been toasted.
explanation.definitionFit: The forehead is one of the facial features.

clue.text: Corporation's the first to make contact with this dive

definitions.text: Corporation's the first to make contact with this dive

parts.words: Corporation's the first to make contact with this dive
parts.note: corporation is old slang for a paunch; in this clumsy dive the stomach hits the water first

explanation.surface: A big company being first to contact a seedy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation is old British slang for a pot belly; dive looks like a seedy bar but is a plunge into a pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive in which the swimmer lands flat on the stomach, the paunch striking the water first.

clue.text: Authoritative point? Annoying alarm's ringing

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the rearranged letters surround the point
annoying means disturbing, so the letters of alarm are stirred up

parts.note: the letters of alarm, the possessive adding none
the gist of something is its main point

explanation.surface: An irritating alarm clock is going off, and someone insists that is the authoritative point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Annoying' rearranges ALARM into MARAL, split around the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Magistral means having the commanding manner of a master or magistrate, so dictatorial.

clue.text: Maybe this shows self-possession, so poses topless

indicators.note: topless says the word loses its top, the first letter

parts.note: a model sits, or poses, for an artist

explanation.surface: A model posing topless shows remarkable self-possession.
explanation.walkthrough: Self-possession is literal: this pronoun is the possessive of it, so it owns 'itself'.
explanation.definitionFit: This possessive pronoun shows belonging to a thing, i.e. the possession of the thing itself.

clue.text: Clay covering used to protect old instrument

definitions.meaning: a cement or clay paste used to seal joints or coat a vessel against fire
a plucked stringed instrument of the Renaissance, with a pear-shaped body

explanation.surface: An old instrument wrapped in clay to keep it safe.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sealing paste of clay and the stringed instrument of early music.

clue.text: Sick women apparently disinherited?

indicators.note: being disinherited means being cut out of the testament, so the women are removed from it

parts.note: apparently hints at the document involved in inheritance, a testament

explanation.surface: Women seem to have been cut off without a penny and feel sick about it.
explanation.walkthrough: To be disinherited is to be written out of a will: take W (women) out of WILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unwell, poorly or ailing is the plain meaning.

clue.text: Plain language quaintly pleasing Sue

parts.note: prose is ordinary language, not verse
cute means attractive in a quaint or sweet way

explanation.surface: A girl called Sue charms with her simple, quaint way of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: Sue looks like a girl's name; it is the verb, to take to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue someone is to bring legal action against them, the same as taking them to court.

clue.text: I don't know — does hospital drama have to be just about acceptable?

parts.note: a quiz contestant who cannot answer says pass
must means have to
ER is the American television hospital drama

explanation.surface: A contestant stumped by a question about whether a TV medical drama is good enough.
explanation.definitionFit: To come up to the required standard, to be passable, is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Source of perfume or repeated riots for dispersal

indicators.note: dispersal scatters things, so the letters are rearranged
repeated says the little word is given twice

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Perfume or repeated riots, with police sent to break them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated' doubles OR; 'for dispersal' then rearranges OROR and RIOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The violet-scented rhizome of an iris is dried and powdered for use in perfumery.

clue.text: Tree's in office of major

parts.note: the elder is a tree, and the possessive gives the s
in, meaning fashionable, is hip

explanation.surface: A tree is being installed in an army major's office.
explanation.walkthrough: Major here is the elder of two, as in a school name, not the army rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Major can mean the senior or older, and the position of an older senior person is the post of an elder.

clue.text: Oriental ready for everyone put in no return

indicators.note: put in says one piece is placed inside the other
return says the word for no is read backwards

parts.note: nay is an old word for no
U is the film certificate for universal, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: An Eastern figure ready for everyone, yet promising nothing in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses NAY to YAN; 'put in' puts U inside it. Ready is cash, money in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready money is cash, and this unit is China's currency, an Eastern cash unit.

clue.text: Is rated doubtful at Newmarket, up and running?

indicators.note: doubtful means uncertain, so the letters are not settled in their order

explanation.surface: A racehorse at Newmarket is rated doubtful to run.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWMARKET is a famous English racecourse; a jockey up is mounted, legs either side.
explanation.definitionFit: A jockey riding a racehorse sits with one leg either side of the mount, straddling it.

clue.text: Reason for Rod Hull's impromptu solo act — to do impressions?

parts.note: Rod Hull was a British entertainer whose act was a puppet ostrich-like bird
if the puppet were late, its master would have to perform alone without it

explanation.surface: Why a puppeteer suddenly had to do impressions alone.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod Hull was a British TV entertainer known for his unruly puppet Emu; the reason for a solo act would be that Emu was late.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate or copy someone, as a mimic does with impressions.

clue.text: Here hide figure with hundred and fifty changes

indicators.note: changes signals one letter swapped for the other

parts.note: an ellipse is a geometrical figure, an oval
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: An instruction to hide a number with some arithmetic changes.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap one L (fifty) in ELLIPSE for C (hundred).
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure or overshadow something, as the moon blocks the sun, is to conceal it.

clue.text: Present-day Roman coin in evidence after thousand-smacker return!

indicators.note: after puts the coin behind the reversed letters
return asks for the two letters to be read backwards

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand and X is a kiss, or smacker
the as was a copper coin of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A modern Roman coin turns up after a big thousand-pound return.
explanation.walkthrough: Smacker is slang for a kiss (X) as well as a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is the day on which presents are given.

clue.text: Who heralds the onset of ceremonial competition for Spooner's material

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the sounds of words

parts.note: a race is a competition

parts.words: Who heralds the onset of ceremonial
parts.note: a bagpiper plays to announce the start of a formal event

explanation.surface: A piper announcing a ceremonial contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap is of vowel sounds: race piper becomes rice paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin edible sheets made from rice or plant pith are used as a baking material.

clue.text: Three hands make it behind

parts.note: a hand is four inches, so three hands make twelve inches, a foot, and a foot is written ft
a hand is four inches, so three hands make twelve inches, a foot, and a foot is written ft

explanation.surface: Three workers can make it from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: A hand, used for horses' height, is four inches; three make a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, towards the stern is the rear, behind.

clue.text: Prince is knave? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means only one half survives, so the second half goes

parts.note: a knave is a rascal, a rogue

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a prince is a scoundrel and gets an emphatic answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'definitely', but here it removes half the word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Ethiopia, the title of a prince or governor is ras.

clue.text: Order (for the benefit of community) antiperspirants — their lack may be manifested thus!

parts.note: thus can mean as, in that way
without deodorant you get BO, body odour

explanation.surface: A council order demanding people use antiperspirants.
explanation.walkthrough: An anti-social behaviour order was a British court order restraining nuisances.
explanation.definitionFit: A British anti-social behaviour order was issued to protect the community from a nuisance.

clue.text: Addresses leading to jolly unpleasant shower

parts.note: to hail someone is to address them
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: Speeches that lead on to a very unpleasant downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: Jolly looks like 'very'; it is old slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A downpour of ice pellets is an unpleasant kind of shower.

clue.text: Well … I'm outstanding!

parts.note: so, like well, opens a sentence
I am, the speaker, is me

explanation.surface: A boastful speaker announces their own brilliance.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'that was some party', the word means remarkable or excellent.

clue.text: Fine ingredient of salad dish set off gumbo

parts.note: OK means fine, all right

indicators.note: set off means removed, so these letters are taken away from the vegetable

parts.note: a radish is a common salad vegetable
taken as written

explanation.surface: A good salad dish is served alongside a Cajun stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine ingredient of salad dish' reads as one phrase, but 'dish' is the part to strike out of the vegetable, with 'set off' as the removal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The green pods of this plant, also called lady's fingers, are known as gumbo in America.

clue.text: Unspeakable assembly is fitting?

definitions.meaning: Wilde called fox hunters the unspeakable in pursuit of the uneatable, so their gathering is a hunt

explanation.surface: A disgraceful gathering is apparently appropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar Wilde called fox-hunting 'the unspeakable in full pursuit of the uneatable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a gathering of a hunt and an archaic adjective for suitable or proper.

clue.text: Opening race leader's disqualified

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a race is an athletic event

explanation.surface: The front-runner is disqualified from the opening race.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlet or aperture through which air or gas escapes.

clue.text: East German resident, back satisfied with frolic, making late inquiry

indicators.note: resident means living inside, so this piece goes in
back says the words are read in reverse

parts.note: met, as in met a demand, means satisfied
a romp is a frolic
Ost is German for east

explanation.surface: An East German living in a house finishes a romp, then starts a late inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: Late here means dead, so the inquiry is into a death.
explanation.definitionFit: An examination of a dead body is an inquiry into the late, i.e. deceased.
